title: Implement R adaptive-rejection sampler with tests
query: Implement an adaptive-rejection sampler as described in Gilks et al. (1992) in R. Save the main implementation in /app/ars.R, with a primary function named ars whose signature is ars(density_function, domain, n = sample_count). The sampler must accept reasonable user inputs, including the number of points to sample, validate inputs (e.g., reject negative sample counts and invalid domains), accept a vectorized function or expression for the possibly unnormalized density (e.g., dnorm), and check for non-log-concave densities during sampling, with clear errors for invalid inputs and non-log-concave densities. Use modular code with auxiliary functions or OOP methods for discrete tasks and consistent style. Include a test function named test that performs formal testing against known distributions and prints results as "TEST_NAME: PASS" or "TEST_NAME: FAIL" with mean and standard deviation statistics. Tests must cover the overall function and any complicated modules, with clear interpretable output despite stochastic results. Ensure ars can generate valid samples from standard distributions such as normal and exponential, with samples following the target distribution shape rather than uniform random values. Generate at least one sample file at /app/normal_samples.txt or /app/exponential_samples.txt containing test samples. Install R if not already available. Reference: Gilks, W. R., & Wild, P. (1992). Adaptive rejection sampling for Gibbs sampling. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series C (Applied Statistics), 41(2), 337-348.
review_flags: The ars signature uses n = sample_count, but sample_count is undefined/ambiguous; confirm the parameter name and intended default.
The expected domain input format is not specified (e.g., numeric bounds versus a call or expression).
The sample-file requirement permits either /app/normal_samples.txt or /app/exponential_samples.txt; confirm whether one is preferred.
